title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the axiomatics of 'polynomial categories' P. In such a category the morphism sets are graded by degree: P_n(X;Y) is the set of maps homogeneous of degree n, and P_{ν1..νr}(X1,...,Xr;Y) is the set of multi-homogeneous maps. The previous page defined 'strict' polynomial categories and '⊗-pd-categories'. A ⊗-pd-category is an additive category with a tensor product ⊗ and divided-power functors Γ^n. For a coproduct X = ∐ X_i, the diagonal Γ^n(X) → ⊗Γ^{ν_i}(X_i) gives a decomposition map from P_n(∏X_i;Y) to the multidegree pieces P_{ν}(X1,...,Xr;Y).

The page completes the definition of a k-linear polynomial category. One asks for a ring map k → End(id_P) such that this diagonal respects the k-grading. Concretely, if f ∈ P_{ν1..νr}, then f∘(λ1·id × ... × λr·id) = λ1^{ν1}...λr^{νr} f for every (λ1,...,λr) ∈ k^r. So multi-homogeneity of degree ν is tested by the scalar action, as for Roby's homogeneous polynomial laws.

Example: the category of k-modules is a ⊗-pd-category. Hence so is the category of K-Modules on a topos X with a ring K. In the bracketed remark, Grothendieck extends this to graded K-Modules, i.e. complexes, by taking Γ^n(M^•) graded by total degree. This is the setting of the cote's title: multiplicative and divided-power structures on ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes, i.e. λ-type operations on perfect complexes.

He then raises a question for the 'abstract' case. How can one put a 'p.d.' structure on Γ^*(M), i.e. a natural law Γ^p(Γ^q(M)) → Γ^{pq}(M) satisfying the divided-power axioms? For modules this is the classical composite γ_p∘γ_q = ((pq)!/(p!(q!)^p)) γ_{pq} on the augmentation ideal of the free divided-power algebra. In modern terms it is the plethysm or composition map of divided-power functors. Grothendieck wants it derived from the axioms of an abstract ⊗-pd-category.

The next page pushes further. Composition of morphisms, and the maps f ↦ Γ^p(f), should be polynomial maps of degree p between Hom-modules, not merely set maps. In effect P should be enriched in polynomial maps, which is what strict polynomial functors / Γ^d-categories later formalise.
errors: The homogeneity condition f∘(λ·id) = λ^ν f, tested only on λ ∈ k, does not determine degree when k is finite (e.g. λ^q = λ on F_q). A correct notion must be functorial in base-change k → k' (Roby polynomial laws) or built into the grading axiomatically. As written, 'respect the grading of k' is weaker than intended unless the grading is part of the structure.

For graded modules / complexes, Γ^n(M^•) 'for the total degree' needs Koszul sign conventions: odd-degree pieces should contribute exterior, not divided, powers. The note does not address this; it may be what the '?' in the margin signals.
The p.d. structure question for Γ^*(M) concerns the augmentation ideal Γ^+(M) (γ_p on Γ^q for q ≥ 1). The phrase 'loi de degré 1' is unclear and possibly mis-stated.

ideas.what: k-linear polynomial category: morphisms graded by (multi)degree, with scalar action giving homogeneity f∘(λ id) = λ^ν f
ideas.modern_name: category enriched in homogeneous polynomial maps; Γ^d-enriched categories / strict polynomial functor categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (polynomial laws, 1963); Friedlander–Suslin (strict polynomial functors, 1997); Kuhn; Krause (Γ^d P categories, 2013)

ideas.what: ⊗-pd-category: additive symmetric monoidal category with divided-power functors Γ^n satisfying exponential/diagonal axioms; k-modules and K-Modules on a topos as examples
ideas.modern_name: symmetric monoidal category with divided power (Γ) structure; exponential functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related ideas in Illusie (Complexe cotangent, simplicial PD), Touzé on exponential functors, Brantner–Mathew on derived divided powers

ideas.what: Divided powers of graded K-Modules (complexes) via total degree, as source of multiplicative structures on perfect complexes
ideas.modern_name: derived divided powers / Dold–Puppe non-additive derived functors / λ-structure on K-theory of perfect complexes
ideas.where_published: SGA6 treats λ-operations on perfect complexes, not this axiomatic route

ideas.what: Question: abstract construction of plethysm Γ^p(Γ^q M) → Γ^{pq} M satisfying PD axioms in a ⊗-pd-category
ideas.modern_name: composition/plethysm of divided-power functors; PD-structure on free divided power algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartan/Roby (classical case); plethysm in strict polynomial functors (Touzé et al.)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates an axiomatic notion of k-linear 'polynomial category' and '⊗-pd-category'. These are categories carrying homogeneous-polynomial morphism sets and divided-power functors. He asks whether the PD composition Γ^pΓ^q → Γ^{pq} can be constructed purely from the axioms. The question is left open here; it is a categorical axiomatisation of divided-power structures predating strict polynomial functors (1997) and Γ^d-enriched categories.
missed.quote: Il y a diverses questions dans le cas "abstrait". Par exemple : comment ... mettre sur Γ^*(M), une structure "à p.d."? i.e. une loi ... Γ^p(Γ^q(M)) → Γ^{pq}(M) satisfaisant aux axiomes des p.d.?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The analogous question for symmetric monoidal (∞-)categories with Γ-structures arises in derived divided-power algebra (Brantner–Mathew, Raksit, derived PD-rings). Grothendieck's axiomatic route is an early instance not credited in that literature.

missed.claim: Divided-power structures on complexes of K-Modules on a topos are linked to multiplicative (λ-type) structures on perfect complexes. The link runs through an abstract polynomial-category formalism, anticipating the later use of strict polynomial functors and derived functors of Γ^n in K-theory and Riemann–Roch contexts.
missed.quote: D'où si X un topos avec une K, la cat. des K-Modules ... K-Modules gradués ... on considère des gradués Γ^n(M^i) pour le degré total
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck around 1975 pursuing a polynomial/PD-enriched categorical framework for operations on perfect complexes, close to modern polynomial-functor approaches to λ-operations.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a fragmentary definition plus an open question. Its interest is historical: an early axiomatics of categories enriched in polynomial maps with divided powers, ~20 years before strict polynomial functors. Mathematically, the classical case is standard.
transcription_corrections: 'co-pd-catégorie' is more likely '⊗-pd-catégorie', matching the term defined on the previous page.
'(VMFD!P1)' is an unreadable interlinear insertion and should be treated as illegible; it is probably not mathematical content.
'peut-on mettre peut-être sur Γ^*(M)' — the image suggests something like 'pt [peut-on] construire ... sur Γ^*(M)'; the sense is 'how can one construct/put a PD structure on Γ^*(M)'.
In the bracket, the line reads roughly 'D ⇒ si X est un topos avec une [k-Algèbre crossed out] K, la cat. des K-Modules'; the struck words are 'k-Algèbre'.
